aep-ohio-dct.collateral: 50% of the total minimum charges for the full term, unless the customer has an A-/A3 credit rating and cash over 10 times the requirement
aep-ohio-dct.exitFee: After the fifth contract year past the ramp, 36 months of minimum charges after notice of termination
aep-ohio-dct.minimum: The greater of 85% of the highest monthly billing demand in the past 11 months, or 15,000 kW plus 85% above 25,000 kW (25,001 to 75,000 kW of contract capacity) or 57,500 kW plus 100% above 75,000 kW (over 75,000 kW), never more than 85% of contract capacity
aep-ohio-dct.ramp: Up to 4 years, at no less than 50%, 65%, 80%, and 90% of contract capacity
aep-ohio-dct.threshold: 25,000 kW or more of data center load, including affiliated loads at one location in aggregate
dominion-gs5.collateral: $1.5 million/MW, reducible by up to 70% for established credit, released 1/14 each year
dominion-gs5.exitFee: Any outstanding minimum charges over the remaining contract term
dominion-gs5.minimum: Distribution 85%, transmission 85%, and generation 60% of contracted demand
dominion-gs5.ramp: Up to 4 years within the term, at least 20% a year
dominion-gs5.threshold: 25 MW or more on a contiguous site, with a load factor of at least 75%
georgia-power-large-load.docket: Docket No. 55378 (the 2024 interim resource plan the rule derives from)
georgia-power-large-load.minimum: Minimum billing is allowed; contracts are filed with the PSC for review, and no formula is published
texas-25-194.collateral: $50,000 per MW of requested peak demand (or of the increase, for an expansion)
texas-25-194.threshold: A new or expanded interconnection at a single site of 75 MW or more, or co-location with a generation resource, for a load not yet energized
